exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted backend traffic can be captured by an attacker performing network sniffing to intercept sensitive data in transit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted backend channels may be exploited to exfiltrate data over alternative protocols without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS configurations can be exploited through downgrade attacks to force use of weaker cipher suites or protocol versions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS configuration directly relates to weakened encryption that adversaries can exploit to decrypt communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Reduce Key Space
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak TLS configurations often involve reduced key lengths, which corresponds to reducing the effective key space attackers need to break.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: An exposed management interface is a public-facing application that adversaries can directly exploit to gain access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Exposed management interfaces typically provide remote service access that adversaries can abuse for lateral movement or initial access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Default Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Default or weak admin credentials directly correspond to the use of default accounts that have not been changed from factory settings.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Password Guessing
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak admin credentials are susceptible to password guessing attacks by adversaries attempting to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, backend communications are vulnerable to adversary-in-the-middle attacks where traffic can be intercepted and manipulated.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing mutual TLS means certificates are not used for backend authentication, enabling certificate forgery attacks to impersonate backend services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Health check endpoints often disclose network configuration and topology information useful for adversary reconnaissance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient access logging relates directly to log management weaknesses that adversaries exploit or benefit from to avoid detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Hide Infrastructure
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient logging enables adversaries to hide their infrastructure and activities by operating in environments with poor visibility.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing rate limiting and connection throttling allows service exhaustion flood attacks to overwhelm the load balancer or backend services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Denial of Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Without connection throttling, the load balancer is vulnerable to network-level denial of service attacks that saturate available resources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of rate limiting enables application-layer exhaustion floods targeting specific application resources through the load balancer.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Proxy
exploitedBy.relevance: Unvalidated forwarded headers can be manipulated by attackers using proxies to spoof source addresses and bypass IP-based access controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
exploitedBy.relevance: Privileged process execution can be exploited to escalate privileges when vulnerabilities exist in processes running with elevated permissions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Create or Modify System Process
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries may abuse privileged process execution contexts to create or modify system processes for persistence or escalation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded secrets in configuration files are directly exploitable as credentials stored in files that adversaries can discover and use.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded secrets often include private keys embedded in configuration files that adversaries can extract for authentication or decryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Hardcoded secrets represent unsecured credentials that adversaries can find and leverage to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched software vulnerabilities in load balancers can be exploited through remote service exploitation techniques.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing MFA on admin interfaces directly corresponds to the absence of multi-factor authentication controls that adversaries can bypass or exploit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
exploitedBy.relevance: When MFA is absent on admin interfaces, adversaries do not need to intercept MFA tokens, making credential-based attacks trivially successful.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credential Stuffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Without MFA, admin interfaces are vulnerable to credential stuffing attacks that can achieve account takeover with stolen credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
exploitedBy.relevance: Sessions without timeout remain valid indefinitely, making stolen session cookies permanently usable for unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Web Session Cookie
exploitedBy.relevance: Long-lived management sessions allow adversaries to use captured web session cookies to maintain persistent unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Remote Service Session Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Without session timeouts, hijacked remote management sessions remain valid, enabling persistent unauthorized control of the load balancer.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Service Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated backend pool auto-discovery exposes network services to enumeration by adversaries performing network service discovery.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Auto-discovery without authentication in cloud environments enables adversaries to enumerate cloud infrastructure components and backend pools.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing certificate monitoring allows adversaries to develop and use fraudulent digital certificates without timely detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Root Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of certificate validity monitoring may allow unauthorized root certificate installation to go undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted ICMP and diagnostic protocols can be abused as non-application layer protocol channels for covert communication or reconnaissance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SNMP (MIB Dump)
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted diagnostic protocols including SNMP allow adversaries to dump MIB data and gather detailed network configuration information.
